requirements.evidence: Locale/name pinned in `.env.example:1,7-8` and `phpunit.xml:21-23`; theme configured at `config/mail.php:128-129` with the brand color `background-color: #0f7490` at `resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:242`; all five named routes and their middleware are at `routes/web.php:16-30`; the reset request always returns `passwords.sent` (`app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-33`); the reset validates the required rules, rotates `remember_token`, fires `PasswordReset` and redirects to `/` with status (`app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:32-57`); verification uses `EmailVerificationRequest` and redirects to `/` (`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:15-19`); the two subject translations are added at `lang/pt_BR.json:559,804`, and `User` implements `MustVerifyEmail` at `app/Models/User.php:15`.

conventions.evidence: Follows Laravel/Pest/Blade style and updates the docs (`CHANGELOG.md:12`, `docs/business-rules.md:137-142`); reuses the framework broker and request classes rather than adding service/repository layers; one clear deviation: `app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:32-36` validates token, e-mail and the complex password rule inline although the convention switches to a `make:request` Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.

security.evidence: Forms use `@csrf` and escaped `{{ }}` output (`resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:31`, `resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:26-27`); e-mail and password are validated server-side (`app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:32-36`); the reset request never branches on user existence (`app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-33`); verification is `auth` + `signed` and `EmailVerificationRequest` enforces id/hash with 403 (`routes/web.php:28-30`, `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:15-19`); no unescaped user output or secrets appear in the diff.

tests.evidence: Three Pest feature files cover the flows: `tests/Feature/PasswordResetTest.php:14-135` (form render, guest-only request page, link sent/unknown/throttle/validation, reset success, invalid token, weak passwords, required fields), `tests/Feature/EmailVerificationTest.php:19-63` (valid link, wrong hash, other id, unsigned link, throttling) and `tests/Feature/MailThemeTest.php:15-47` (locale/name, theme, translated and branded reset/verification mail). Gaps remain: guest-only behavior is only tested for `password.request`, and the new welcome status flash and the verification mail's `PegaFila` name are unasserted.

simplicity.evidence: Uses Laravel's built-in `Password` broker, `EmailVerificationRequest` and notifications instead of custom services (`app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:38-56`, `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:17-19`); the two auth views duplicate the same head/fonts/vite/Bulma and body shell (`resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-18`, `resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:1-18`), which is the only notable duplication.

readability.evidence: Small, focused methods with docblocks and clear names (`app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetLinkController.php:13-34`, `app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:14-57`, `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:8-20`); views use consistent Bulma markup and accessible labels; no dead code, debug output or inconsistent style in the diff.

scope.evidence: The diff is limited to the locale/test pins, mail config/theme, routes, controllers, views, lang, the `User` verification interface, the docs and a small welcome status block that makes the `password.update` flash visible (`resources/views/welcome.blade.php:20-22`); no login, registration, `/home`, Livewire, SCSS/JS or unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: Token, e-mail and the complex password rule are validated inline in the controller, but the conventions ask for a `make:request` Form Request once validation grows beyond one or two fields, which is the case here.

The guest-only restriction is asserted only for `password.request`; the reset GET/POST routes are also under `guest` and the newly added welcome status flash has no test, so part of the required behavior is unverified.
Both pages repeat the same head/fonts/vite/Bulma and body shell; a small anonymous Blade component or partial would remove the duplication, although the impact is low with only two pages.

review.summary: The change implements the pt-BR PegaFila account e-mails end to end: locale pins, the custom `pegafila` mail theme, translated notification subjects, the guest-only password-reset flow, the signed verification route and broad Pest coverage. It is idiomatic Laravel and secure, with no blockers; the nits are inline validation instead of a Form Request, duplicated auth-page shells, and a few missing test assertions for the guest-only reset routes and the welcome flash. Approve with those nits.
